minutes.headline: Planning Board approved the Verizon school-site monopole with construction-hour limits, then interviewed two applicants for a vacancy.
minutes.summary: The board accepted a minor Unitil parking change, waived the balloon float, and approved the Verizon monopole at 1079 Mass Ave with conditions on construction hours and compliance with other boards. It interviewed two applicants for the vacant seat, ahead of a joint meeting with the Selectmen. The director reviewed the subsidized housing inventory, and the board agreed a new comment process for bylaw review.

public_comment.topic: Questions on the Verizon tower: radiation, other tenants, and lease revenue compared with the Town Hall tower lease.
School department director clarified that the track and field are under the Parks Commission and the lease money goes to the town.

votes.motion: Accept the Unitil changes as outlined in the plan
Grant the waiver of the balloon float
Close the public hearing on the Verizon monopole
Approve the Verizon monopole with construction-hours and meet-all-boards conditions

budget_items.topic: Verizon lease rent to the town
budget_items.what_was_said: Counsel described the annual rent and annual escalator starting after the building permit issues.
A resident worried colocation could cost the town revenue compared with the existing Town Hall lease.
Lease money is expected to go to the high school track and field project, though the warrant articles are not formally tied.

decisions.decision: Members will send bylaw comments to the director by Tuesday start of business so he can compile them into the packet.
Joint meeting with the Selectmen set for July 18 to fill the vacancy.
Director to arrange for new town counsel to come speak on host community agreements.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted to approve the Verizon monopole at 1079 Mass Ave, with conditions on construction hours and compliance with other boards.
Before that vote, the board waived the balloon float and closed the public hearing on the monopole.
Residents asked about radiation, other tenants and lease revenue; counsel described annual rent and an escalator that starts after the building permit issues.
The board interviewed two applicants for the vacant seat and set a joint meeting with the Selectmen on July 18 to fill it.
Members agreed to send bylaw comments to the director by Tuesday start of business, to be compiled into the packet.

why_it_matters: The approval allows a new cell tower on a school site, and the lease rent it brings the town is expected to go toward the high school track and field project, though the warrant articles are not formally tied.
The vacancy appointment and the bylaw review process decide who sits on the board and how zoning changes are shaped before residents are asked to vote on them.
watch_next: Joint meeting of the Planning Board and Selectmen on July 18 to fill the board vacancy.
Compiled bylaw comments in the packet, and new town counsel speaking on host community agreements.
